subject: Genetics
title: Craig Venter's Gamble
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Craig Venter's Gamble.

hook.text: In 1998, a maverick scientist said he'd sequence the genome faster and cheaper than the government. Alone.

buildup.text: Craig Venter founded Celera Genomics with private funding. He promised to finish by 2001—years ahead of schedule.

discovery.text: Venter used shotgun sequencing: blast the genome into fragments, read them all, then use computers to reassemble.

twist.text: The public project panicked and accelerated. Competition drove both teams to work harder and faster than planned.

climax.text: The race transformed genomics. What was planned for 15 years finished in 13. Rivalry outpaced the timeline.

punchline.text: Competition did what funding alone couldn't: it sped up history.

quiz.question: What sequencing method did Craig Venter's Celera use?
